subject: Acme renewal & expansion - call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme renewal & expansion - call recap

Alex / Samantha — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Summary of what we heard
- Current pain: production latency spikes and unpredictable token costs on peak batch workloads (customer search and support routing).
- Goal: lock in predictable cost and improve 95th percentile latency to <= 120ms for the search flow by the start of Q3.
- Usage snapshot: you’re currently at ~1.2M tokens/day with two main workloads (search ranking + conversational assistance).

Proposed expansion path
1) Add Redwood Dedicated pool for search-routing workload (pin a 2-GPU pool) — reduces latency and gives capacity isolation.
2) Use prefix/KV caching and quantized model variant for conversational assistance to cut unit cost ~30%.
3) 90-day pilot: measure latency and cost delta, then move to a 6- or 12-month reserved commit depending on results.

Open questions we asked you to confirm
- Which internal SLA target (latency/cost) should we use as the success metric?
- Are there compliance or procurement timelines we should be aware of for Q3 commit?

Next steps / Asks
- Marissa: will share the Q1 usage export and a preliminary pricing proposal (by EOD Friday).
- Alex: please confirm preferred SLA target and any procurement contacts we should loop in.
- Redwood: schedule a short follow-up to walk through the usage report and pricing details (30 min).

Attachment: I’ll attach a CSV export of the usage and a one-page pricing sketch in the follow-up.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
--
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Reyes <samantha.reyes@acme.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme renewal & expansion - call recap

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. That matches our internal readout. A few clarifications: 
- SLA: target 95th percentile latency of 120ms for search, as you noted.
- Procurement: procurement will need a 30-day review; I’ll introduce you to our procurement lead, Samantha (cc’d).
- Budget: we have an internal target to keep monthly cloud spend growth under 15% YoY, so any committed pricing will need to show a clear unit-cost win compared to our current setup.

We’ll review the usage export when you send it. Can you include a line-item showing expected savings from the caching + quantized model variant? That will help with procurement.

Alex
Director of Engineering, Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Marissa — adding a quick internal note on options we should push in the pricing doc: 
- Pilot pricing: 60-day discounted reserved capacity rate for the Dedicated pool with a one-time onboarding credit.
- Post-pilot: two commit options (6-month and 12-month) with ascending discounts tied to committed QPS.
- Technical note: recommend we include an explicit fallback plan to hosted variants for non-critical routes if their Dedicated pool needs maintenance — this reduces risk during the pilot.

I’ll draft the line items and share a first pass of the pricing PDF tomorrow.

—Michael

Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme renewal & expansion - call recap

Alex / Samantha — attaching the Q1 usage export and the proposed pricing PDF for the pilot (stubs below).

Attachments:
- acme_q1_usage.csv (export of token counts by route and hour)
- proposed-pricing.pdf (first-pass pricing & pilot terms)

Quick summary of the attachment highlights:
- Baseline: ~1.2M tokens/day; search routing peaks at 2k QPS during PST morning window.
- Estimated savings: caching + quantized model variant = ~28–34% reduction in unit cost in our simulation; Dedicated pool should remove 95th percentile latency spikes for search.
- Pilot ask: start the 60-day pilot by March 1, decision point by April 30 for a commit.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Alex to introduce procurement contact and confirm SLA target (by Mon 2/15).
2) Marissa & Michael to schedule a 30-minute walk-through of the usage export and pricing (propose 2/16 or 2/17).
3) Redwood to share a final pilot statement of work and reserved capacity term sheet after walk-through.

Let me know what timing works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot running.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
